text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.7% today to $427.34, continuing a two-week decline of 10%. The stock was pressured on the heels of quarterly earnings and financial reports released today, which investors are still digesting. Additionally, energy markets have shifted: US crude dropped below $104 per barrel while global crude trades at $123, and refineries are running at 92.8% capacity — solid but not stretched. A leadership change at the company also accompanied today's reporting.

The broader energy sector has been cautious heading into this earnings season. Analysts flagged last week that while Big Oil earnings are expected to be strong, forward guidance will be the real driver of stock moves — and today's combination of results, management transition, and soft refining margins (the gap between crude costs and refined product prices) appears to have disappointed rather than excited investors.
